reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that organismic behavior under reinforcement is governed by a dual mechanism: (1) summation of stimulus habit strengths, and (2) probabilistic evaluation against a reaction threshold. The former enables a first-order approximation to adaptive probability via \( \sum s_i + \sum \hat{s}_{ij} \), while the latter introduces stochasticity through \( \sigma(\theta \cdot (\sum s_i - \tau)) \). As training progresses, habit strength accumulates according to \( \frac{dH}{dt} = \alpha \cdot \mathbb{P}(R|S) \cdot (1 - H) \), improving decision accuracy. These primitives form a closed-loop system where perception (stimulus) → cognition (habit) → action (gamble) → feedback (reinforcement). Failure modes include overfitting to cues, underestimating interaction effects, and premature convergence to suboptimal policies. The system exhibits robustness through thresholding and cumulative learning but is sensitive to environmental shifts.
